tone_statements.quote: 62. NOT [...] ǁXegwi: Ziervogel 1955: 43, 53; Lanham & Hallowes 1956: 114. Said by Ziervogel to be pronounced with high tone, as opposed to ʔa 'thou' q.v. with low tone. [...] 87. THOU [...] ǁXegwi: Ziervogel 1955: 46. Said to be pronounced with low tone, as opposed to ʔa 'not' q.v. with high tone [Ziervogel 1955: 43].
tone_statements.locator: p. 46, entry 62 'not' (ǁXegwi note) and p. 61, entry 87 'thou' (ǁXegwi note); cf. p. 62, entry 90 'tree' (ǁXegwi note: Lanham & Hallowes 1956: 106 form -zì 'with specially marked low tone')
tone_statements.summary: Secondhand from Ziervogel 1955 (and Lanham & Hallowes 1956): ǁXegwi had lexically distinctive tone, with at least a high vs low contrast shown by the minimal pair ʔa 'not' (high) vs ʔa 'thou' (low); the number of tones, tone-bearing unit and any grammatical role are not described in this work.

sources.note: Only a general remark that the Tuu/Kx'a/Khoe sprachbund languages 'all.. have tone'; nothing on stress or on ǁXegwi specifically.

Phonology > Tone: 'From Köhler's material, it appears that ǁXʼegwi had a four-tone inventory.' (unsourced in the wikitext; the article's phonology cites Honken 2020 and Traill 1999). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bleek, Dorothea F. 1956. A Bushman Dictionary. American Oriental Series 41. New Haven: American Oriental Society. (SIII = 'batwa, Lake Chrissie, eastern Transvaal', D.F. Bleek's own pre-WWI field data)
sources.note: Introduction lists SIII = batwa of Lake Chrissie and notes Miss Bleek 'visited Lake Chrissie in the eastern Transvaal to sample that of the Batwa'. No statement on stress for SIII or any language; only a general remark under the letter a: 'Some variations in tone and length have been noted, doubtless others have not been heard and recorded.' Dictionary entries for SIII carry no stress marks or discussion.

sources.note: No description of the tone system; annotated 110-item list. Two notes relay first-hand tone marking in Ziervogel 1955: p. 46 ('not'): 'ǁXegwi: Ziervogel 1955: 43, 53; Lanham & Hallowes 1956: 114. Said by Ziervogel to be pronounced with high tone, as opposed to ʔa 'thou' q.v. with low tone.' and p. 61 ('thou'): 'ǁXegwi: Ziervogel 1955: 46. Said to be pronounced with low tone, as opposed to ʔa 'not' q.v. with high tone [Ziervogel 1955: 43].' -> evidence that Ziervogel 1955 (our print-only row) records a lexical high/low tone contrast; tone marks in the list itself are data, not a statement.
